title: Employee Handbook

text: This handbook introduces the working principles, policy framework, and support pathways used by Promote Health Analytics Pty Ltd. It helps employees locate authoritative policies and understand how responsibilities are shared across employees, managers, People and Culture, Information Security, and Finance.
title: Employee Handbook

text: This handbook applies to employees, contractors, managers, and leaders. It is a navigational and cultural document. It does not replace the detailed requirements in the authoritative policies listed in the Related Documents section.
title: Employee Handbook

title: Employee Handbook

text:
Employees should consult the relevant authoritative policy before relying on a summary, informal message, or prior practice.

Managers must apply policy consistently and must escalate uncertainty rather than creating local exceptions.

Policy summaries in this handbook are orientation aids only and must not be used as the sole source for a detailed entitlement or approval decision.
title: Employee Handbook

text:
All workers must contribute to a respectful, inclusive, and safe workplace.

All workers must protect confidential information and use company systems only for authorised purposes.

Concerns involving harassment, discrimination, retaliation, threats, or significant security risk must be escalated through the appropriate formal channel.
title: Employee Handbook

text:
Employees must keep their contact, manager, and work-location information current.

Employees must provide accurate information when requesting leave, remote work, reimbursement, benefits support, equipment, or HR assistance.

Employees must obtain required approval before committing the company to travel, expense, or operational obligations.
title: Employee Handbook

text:
Use HR-POL-002 for paid time off and planned annual leave.

Use HR-POL-004 for remote and flexible work, including overseas arrangements.

Use HR-POL-005 for information-security and acceptable-use requirements.

Use HR-POL-013 when a request requires an HR ticket, documented escalation, or a mock action.
title: Employee Handbook

text:
An employee should first provide the relevant employee ID, request type, requested dates or location, and any immediate deadline.

The system may retrieve policy evidence and employee-specific mock data before presenting a response.

Where the evidence is incomplete, the employee should contact People and Culture instead of relying on an unsupported conclusion.
title: Employee Handbook

text:
Employees should begin with the policy whose title most closely matches the request. A paid-time-off question belongs in the Paid Time Off Policy, while an unplanned health-related absence belongs in the Leave and Absence Policy. Where a request spans more than one policy, the response should identify the role of each document instead of blending their rules into one unsupported summary.

A policy title, section heading, and supporting passage should accompany each material policy claim. This approach allows the employee to distinguish an authoritative rule from general guidance, an example, or a suggested next step. A citation must not be attached to a claim that the cited passage does not actually support.
title: Employee Handbook

text:
Employees should rely on the current active policy version. Drafts, superseded documents, informal team notes, and historical practices do not override an active policy. People and Culture coordinates changes and communicates material updates through approved channels.

Questions created by a policy change should be resolved using the effective date, the date of the employee event, and any documented transition arrangement. The handbook does not create a transition rule on its own.
title: Employee Handbook

text: This policy defines how eligible employees of Promote Health Analytics Pty Ltd accrue, request, approve, record, and use paid time off. It establishes the authoritative rules for planned annual leave and related approval decisions.
title: Paid Time Off Policy

text: This policy applies to full-time and part-time employees, including employees in probation. Contractors do not accrue paid time off unless a written contract expressly provides an equivalent benefit.
title: Paid Time Off Policy

text: Paid planned leave recorded against an employee's available balance. Common aliases include PTO, annual leave, and vacation leave.
title: Paid Time Off Policy

title: Paid Time Off Policy

title: Paid Time Off Policy

text:
Full-time employees receive 20 days of paid time off each year.

Entitlement accrues progressively across the year and is recorded in the employee's paid-time-off balance.

An employee must not represent projected future accrual as currently available leave unless the manager and People and Culture approve an advance arrangement.
title: Paid Time Off Policy

text:
Part-time employees receive a pro-rata entitlement based on their recorded full-time-equivalent fraction.

A change in scheduled hours applies prospectively and must not be used to retrospectively recalculate leave already taken.
title: Paid Time Off Policy

text:
Employees in probation accrue paid time off under the same employment-type rule as other eligible employees.

A probationary employee may request paid time off, but the manager may consider onboarding, training, and operational coverage when deciding the timing.
title: Paid Time Off Policy

text:
An employee must have at least the requested number of available paid-time-off days before a request can be approved as paid leave.

A request with insufficient balance may be discussed as unpaid leave under HR-POL-010 Leave and Absence Policy, but it must not be recorded as paid time off.
title: Paid Time Off Policy

text:
The employee must provide the requested dates, number of workdays, and any relevant operational context.

The employee should verify the available balance before submitting the request.
title: Paid Time Off Policy

text:
Employees should submit planned paid-time-off requests at least 10 calendar days before leave begins.

A shorter-notice request may still be considered where the manager can maintain operational coverage.

Short notice does not remove the requirement for sufficient balance or written manager approval.
title: Paid Time Off Policy

text:
Paid time off requires sufficient available balance and written manager approval.

Managers may approve, decline, or propose alternative dates after considering operational coverage, overlapping leave, deadlines, and critical responsibilities.

Approval is not effective until it is recorded in the approved leave process.
title: Paid Time Off Policy

text:
An employee must notify the manager promptly if approved dates change.

A cancellation returns unused approved days to the employee's available balance after the record is updated.
title: Paid Time Off Policy

text:
Employees should discuss foreseeable extended leave early enough for the manager to plan handover, customer coverage, scheduled work, and critical responsibilities. The discussion supports operational planning but does not replace the formal request or approval record.

Managers should assess requests using consistent factors rather than personal preference. Relevant factors may include overlapping approved leave, critical deadlines, minimum service coverage, regulatory commitments, and the practicality of temporary task reassignment. A manager should explain a declined or altered request in clear operational terms.
title: Paid Time Off Policy

text:
An employee who believes the displayed balance is incorrect should raise the discrepancy before relying on the balance. People and Culture may review accrual history, prior leave records, employment type, changes in work fraction, and corrections.

A balance correction does not by itself approve a pending leave request. After the corrected balance is confirmed, the manager must still decide the request under the approval conditions in this policy.
title: Paid Time Off Policy

text:
A request for an extended period should include a practical handover plan and sufficient time for operational review. The company may discuss alternative dates or a staged arrangement where the requested period would create a material service or delivery risk.

The existence of sufficient balance does not guarantee approval of a specific period. The manager should nevertheless consider the employee's ability to take meaningful breaks and should avoid repeatedly deferring reasonable requests without a documented operational basis.
title: Paid Time Off Policy

text:

text: This policy defines the conditions under which employees of Promote Health Analytics Pty Ltd may work remotely or use a flexible work arrangement. It is the authoritative source for domestic and international remote-work eligibility, duration, notice, and approval.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text: This policy applies to employees whose duties can be performed away from a company office. Contractors must follow their contract and the same information-security controls when accessing company systems.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text: Authorised work performed away from the employee's assigned company office. Common aliases include working from home and WFH.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text: Remote work performed within Australia from an approved location.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text: Remote work performed outside Australia for a temporary period.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text: The office or approved location recorded in the employee profile.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text:
Remote work is available only where duties, performance, confidentiality, team coordination, and service obligations can be maintained.

A remote-work arrangement does not change the employee's role, manager, or assigned location unless a formal change is approved.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text:
Domestic remote work may be approved by the manager under an established team arrangement.

The employee must maintain a safe, private, and reliable work environment and remain available during agreed working hours.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text:
Employees in probation may use remote work where the manager confirms that onboarding, supervision, and role learning can be maintained.

A manager may require additional office attendance where performance support, collaboration, or operational need justifies it.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text:
International remote work is limited to 30 calendar days in any rolling 12-month period.

A proposal for six weeks exceeds the standard limit and is not compliant under the ordinary approval pathway.

An exception requires formal executive review after manager, People and Culture, Information Security, and location-risk assessment.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text:
Employees must not work from a destination identified as restricted by Information Security or the travel and work-location risk process.

The company may decline a destination because of confidentiality, connectivity, sanctions, tax, immigration, employment-location, insurance, or personal-safety concerns.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text:
The employee must provide the proposed country, city, dates, working hours, accommodation type, connectivity plan, and business reason.

The request must identify any access to health, customer, employee, financial, or other confidential information.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text:
International remote-work requests should be submitted at least 20 calendar days before departure.

A shorter-notice request may be reviewed only where the employee documents why normal notice was not possible.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text:
International remote work requires written approval from the manager and People and Culture before travel is booked.

Information Security and location-risk review must be completed where the employee will access company systems overseas.

Approval is not effective until all required reviews are documented.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text:
The employee must maintain agreed working hours, attendance, communication, and performance.

The employee remains responsible for lawful entry, appropriate accommodation, and personal travel arrangements.

The company does not reimburse personal travel or accommodation unless separately approved as business travel.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text:
The employee must obtain further approval before changing the destination, extending the dates, or materially changing the work arrangement.

The company may withdraw approval where security, legal, operational, or safety conditions change.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text:
The employee must maintain a workspace that supports confidentiality, reliable communication, and safe performance of the role. Background noise, shared accommodation, public areas, or unstable connectivity may make a proposed location unsuitable for work involving confidential discussions or time-critical service.

The employee and manager should agree on working hours, time-zone overlap, meeting attendance, response expectations, and handover arrangements. The arrangement must not shift unreasonable coordination burdens to colleagues or reduce required service coverage.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text:
People and Culture may review whether the proposed location creates employment, payroll, tax, insurance, immigration, or right-to-work concerns. The employee must provide accurate destination and duration information and must not represent a personal visitor status as permission to perform company work.

The review is an internal company risk assessment and does not constitute personal immigration or tax advice. The employee remains responsible for obtaining independent advice where needed for personal travel arrangements.
title: Remote and Flexible Work Policy

text:
The company may require the employee to stop overseas work or return to the assigned location where security, safety, legal, operational, performance, or connectivity conditions materially deteriorate. The manager and People and Culture should communicate the reason and the required transition.

An employee who cannot continue under the approved conditions must stop company-system access where directed and contact the manager promptly.

text:
Workers must communicate professionally and must not engage in bullying, harassment, discrimination, retaliation, threats, or deliberate humiliation.

Feedback and performance discussions must address work and behaviour rather than personal attacks.

text:

Managers must maintain appropriate professional boundaries and must avoid retaliation or perceived retaliation.

text:

A worker must not distribute offensive, confidential, or misleading material through company channels.
title: Workplace Conduct Policy

text:
A person may raise a concern in good faith without needing to prove the complete case before seeking support.

Knowingly false or malicious allegations are inconsistent with this policy, but an unsubstantiated concern is not automatically malicious.

A concern may be raised with a manager, People and Culture, or another identified escalation contact.

text:

The system must not invent a missing employee ID or silently substitute another employee.

section_path: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure
text:
Policy guidance must identify the authoritative document and section supporting each material claim.

Where policy evidence is absent or insufficient, the response must state the limitation and recommend People and Culture review.
title: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure

text:
Harassment, discrimination, retaliation, medical, safety, and other sensitive matters must be routed for human review.

The system must not determine credibility, legal liability, diagnosis, or disciplinary outcome.
title: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure

section_path: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure
text:
A request should contain only the information necessary to provide guidance or route the matter.

Sensitive details should not be repeated unnecessarily in summaries or traces.
title: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure

section_path: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure
text:
Identify whether the request needs policy retrieval, employee data, a calculation, clarification, escalation, or a mock action.

If essential information is ambiguous, ask one concise clarifying question.
title: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure

section_path: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure
text:
Retrieve authoritative policy evidence and, where relevant, retrieve employee-specific mock data through MCP tools.

The agent must not directly access the RAG index or mock files outside the MCP tool path.
title: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure

section_path: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure
text:
Before creating a mock ticket or draft message, present the tool name, arguments, and human-readable preview.

The preview must clearly state that the action is mock and does not send a real email or create a real external case.
title: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure

section_path: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure
text:
Mock HR actions require an explicit user confirmation before execution.

Confirmation must match the pending action and its confirmation identifier.

A missing, stale, or mismatched confirmation must not execute the action.
title: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure

section_path: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure
text:
The final response should state the policy basis, employee-specific facts used, action result, and any remaining next step.

The operational trace records tool names, arguments, result summaries, sources, and decisions without exposing hidden chain-of-thought.
title: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure

section_path: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure
text:
Requests should be classified by subject, urgency, sensitivity, and assigned responsible team. A routine balance question differs from a policy exception, a security incident, or a sensitive workplace concern.

Urgency should be based on a specific deadline, safety risk, payroll or benefits impact, access failure, or operational consequence rather than the requester's preference alone.
title: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure

section_path: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure
text:
The case summary should distinguish confirmed facts, requester statements, retrieved records, policy evidence, and unresolved questions. It must not present an allegation or assumption as a verified fact.

Where a correction is made, the updated record should preserve enough context to understand what changed and why.
title: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure

section_path: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure
text:
A case transferred to another owner should include the category, relevant policy references, actions completed, outstanding questions, and requested next step. Sensitive details should be minimised.

A request may be closed when the answer or mock action is complete, the matter has been handed to the responsible human owner, or the requester does not provide required information after an appropriate follow-up.
title: HR Requests and Case Management Procedure
